Within fpt or ghec, the availability fragment declares public repositories eligible by default; its containing feature must be identified by placement.
Setting order can differ between original bundled Advanced Security licensing and separate-product licensing.
Setting names can differ between these license arrangements.
The two separate licensed products are Code Security and Secret Protection.
The source suggests reviewing enterprise settings to identify Advanced Security product licensing.
The fpt-or-ghec branch includes the budgets reference.
Inside that branch, ghec additionally includes the enterprise security-policy reference.
The ghes branch instead links to the Enterprise Cloud-qualified budgets route.
The ghes branch explicitly identifies the linked documentation as Enterprise Cloud documentation.
Some languages may require advanced code-scanning setup for full code coverage.
Some build systems may require advanced setup for full coverage.
Advanced setup is described as requiring substantially more configuration effort.
Advanced setup is also described as requiring more customization effort.
Advanced setup is also described as requiring more maintenance effort.
The source recommends enabling default setup first.
The feature description associates Advanced Security with improving code security.
It also associates those features with maintaining code security.
It associates those features with improving code quality.
It also associates those features with maintaining code quality.
The fragment unconditionally incorporates the security-product bullet-list dependency.
Within ghec or ghes, the alternative Advanced Security license described by the fragment includes all Secret Protection features.
Within the same branch, that alternative license is described as including all Code Security features.
Secret Protection features are described as helping detect secret leaks.
Secret Protection features are also described as helping prevent secret leaks.
Secret scanning is one named Secret Protection feature.
Push protection is another named Secret Protection feature.
Code Security features are described as helping find vulnerabilities.
Code Security features are also described as helping fix vulnerabilities.
Code scanning is one named Code Security feature.
Premium Dependabot capabilities are another named Code Security feature.
Dependency review is another named Code Security feature.
In fpt, the permission fragment identifies owners of eligible Team organizations.
The else branch identifies enterprise owners; it is not explicitly limited to a ghec predicate.
The else branch states that otherwise an Enterprise Cloud trial with Advanced Security is needed.
The ghec branch points to guidance about trying Advanced Security free of charge.
The following fpt branch points to guidance about a free Enterprise trial including Advanced Security.
The fpt branch qualifies both linked guides as Enterprise Cloud documentation.
This reusable has no final fallback branch after ghec and fpt.
The fragment is a further-information reference, not an independent eligibility or approval statement.
The source purchase procedure instructs confirmation of billing information.
The source purchase procedure also instructs confirmation of the payment method.
The next source step is clicking Purchase Advanced Security; importing this instruction does not authorize spending.
Volume/subscription billing requires specifying the number of licenses to purchase.
The quantity step instructs entering the number of committers to license in the indicated input.
In the ghes branch, some security features are described as available for all repositories.
The subsequent fpt-or-ghec branch describes some features as available in repositories on all plans.
Additional features are described for organizations using the referenced security-product combination.
Additional features are also described for enterprises using that combination.
Within fpt or ghec, Advanced Security features are described as enabled for all public repositories.
The further-information reusable is incorporated outside the version-specific clauses.
Security overview summarizes organizational security at a high level.
It also summarizes enterprise security at a high level.
The description frames overview as helping identify repositories requiring intervention.
The Overview summary view shows default-alert data only.
The Coverage summary view shows default-alert data only.
The Risk summary view shows default-alert data only.
Secret-scanning alerts from ignored directories are omitted from the summary views.
Generic secret-scanning alerts are also omitted from these summary views.
Individual alert views can consequently contain more open alerts.
Individual alert views can also contain more closed alerts.
The navigation procedure starts in the sidebar Requests section.
The source offers a secret-scanning alert-dismissal view.
The source separately offers a code-scanning alert-dismissal view.
The Dependabot alert-dismissal option is included only under dependabot-delegated-alert-dismissal.
The reusable points to dashboard-filter documentation without claiming those linked instructions have been reviewed.
The fragment describes downloading CSV data from several organizational security-overview pages.
The enterprise-download wording is included only under security-overview-export-data.
The description identifies security research as a possible CSV use.
It identifies detailed data analysis as another possible use.
It describes integration of these files with external datasets.
The owner search filter is described as selecting data by organization.
Within ghec, an owner of a managed-user enterprise may filter by repository owner type using owner-type.
Under that stated condition, owner-type can select organization-owned repository data.
Under that stated condition, owner-type can alternatively select user-owned repository data.
The source instructs using top-of-page filters to select the alert group for displayed metrics.
The fragment states that all page data change with filter adjustments.
The fragment separately states that all page metrics change with filter adjustments.
The date picker sets the time range for alert activity.
The date picker also sets the metric time range.
The search box adds further filters for displayed alerts.
The search box also filters displayed metrics.
The referenced screenshot's alternative text identifies outlined date-picker filtering.
The alternative text also identifies outlined search-field filtering; no binary visual review is implied.
The source describes top-of-page filters selecting the group of repositories for secret-scanning metrics.
The date picker selects the metric time range.
The date picker date corresponds to when a secret was bypassed, not an unspecified detection date.
The search box adds further secret-scanning metric filters.
The source instructs clicking Scan your organization to generate code-security risk assessment.
If no security risk assessment was previously run, this action also initiates secret risk assessment.
The source instructs clicking Scan your organization to generate secret risk assessment.
If no security risk assessment was previously run, this action also initiates code-security risk assessment.
Overview information varies with repository access.
It also varies with organization access.
It varies with repository use of Advanced Security features.
It also varies with organizational use of those features.
The source instructs opening Assessments under Security in the sidebar.
The source instructs clicking sidebar Risk to display the Security risk view.

The reviewer is instructed to read alert contents.
The reviewer is also instructed to read the requester's dismissal rationale.
The source instructs choosing Review request in the alert timeline.
